The root cause is the decisions made by the industry.  The lowest frequency tested for is 125Hz. Thats mid bass at best. And thusly 125Hz is the lowest audio band hearing aids can adjust.  Hearing aids don’t reproduce sounds over about 8k to 12k depending on the make model, and they all roll off at about 125Hz and below.

Could they do better - especially in bass?  Absolutely, but the industry just hasn’t done so.  I expect with streaming to hearing aids becoming so standard, such is likely to happen.

They have to be, OP. There are several sort of “baseline” standards most hearing aids use, with weird names like NAL-NL2 or DSL 5, etc. Some hearing aid makers also have their own proprietary versions. 

And this is where the audiologist tries to adjust your devices so that your hearing loss frequencies get boosted to fit the ideal curve of the “correct” standard baseline without causing feedback. 

But of course it’s never a perfect fit because hearing is unique to each person! We are all going to deviate in some ways from this “standard ideal.” 

This is why we have to refine them over time as we adjust to the hearing aids & realize “oh this thing doesn’t quite work for me; I need a tweak

When you go for your fitting be sure to have a list of questions for your audi. It helps them to help you if they have an idea what your needs are. As a new user there's a lot to learn, and your brain needs to adjust to the change in your audible environment. Some people take weeks, or even months to adapt, but don't get discouraged, and keep a journal of issues going for your follow up appointment.
